scope: Static clause checks and manually reviewed activation examples; not measured model activation.

polars.original_description: Write fast, idiomatic Polars in Python using the lazy API, and answer natural-language questions about data in one shot. Use this skill whenever a task involves loading, querying, transforming, aggregating, joining, or analyzing tabular data (CSV, Parquet, NDJSON, or DataFrames). top-k, trends, period-over-period, distributions, time series, share-of-total, or writing, debugging, or speeding up Polars code, or translating pandas to Polars. Applies even when the user doesn't say "Polars," and is the default for Python data work when no dataframe library is specified. Covers expressions, window functions, group-bys, joins, the streaming engine for larger-than-memory data, and pandas migration. Not for Polars Cloud, On-Prem, distributed, or GPU workloads.
positive_prompts: Analyze this CSV in Python; choose the library.
Optimize this Polars join.
negative_prompts: Configure Polars On-Prem.
Run a Polars GPU workload.

ctx.original_description: Use ctx as working memory for prior agent work. Before starting or continuing work in an unfamiliar area, resuming earlier work, or revisiting an investigation, search prior sessions to ground yourself in earlier context. When ctx blame is available, use it to trace a line, file, commit, or PR to the agent session that produced it. Use when prior decisions, constraints, attempts, tool calls, transcript evidence, or code provenance may matter.
required_patterns: before starting or continuing unfamiliar work
positive_prompts: Begin work in this unfamiliar subsystem.
Revisit our earlier investigation.
negative_prompts: Answer a standalone arithmetic question with no project history.

track-findings.original_description: Track validated Codex Security findings in Linear, Jira, GitHub issues, or draft GitHub security advisories. Use it for one finding or an explicitly selected batch of up to 25 findings tracked as Linear, Jira, or GitHub issues. Includes duplicate checks, exact previews, approval-gated writes, and readback. Do not use it for scans or fixes.
positive_prompts: Track these 25 validated security findings.
negative_prompts: Track all 40 findings in one batch.
Find and fix vulnerabilities.

ask.original_description: Use when the user asks to be interviewed to clarify a task, or missing purpose, audience, success criteria, or binding constraints prevent useful planning or implementation. Use grilling for an explicit adversarial stress-test of a plan; do not trigger for clear mechanical requests, non-interactive runs, or customer research.
required_patterns: Route adversarial plan reviews to grill
positive_prompts: Interview me to clarify this task.
negative_prompts: Run this mechanical migration unattended.

pgopt.original_description: PostgreSQL-specific development assistant focusing on unique PostgreSQL features, advanced data types, and PostgreSQL-exclusive capabilities. Covers JSONB operations, array types, custom types, range/geometric types, full-text search, window functions, and PostgreSQL extensions ecosystem.
positive_prompts: Implement PostgreSQL full-text search.
negative_prompts: Design a Redis key layout.

recall.original_description: Reconstruct your recent working context from your own chat history, live state, and the shared record (user reports, prior fixes, incidents), then hand back a tight current-state brief. Use for 'recall my work on X', 'catch me up', 'what have I been working on', 'where did I leave off', before starting or resuming work.
positive_prompts: Before starting, reconstruct my recent work.
negative_prompts: Calculate a number with no work context.

skillrev.original_description: Use when the user asks to review or audit an AI-agent skill, investigate its activation, assess its readiness or value, or design or interpret trigger and task-quality evaluations. Do not trigger for ordinary code, PR, security, API-schema, or performance reviews. Review-only requests do not authorize edits; apply improvements only when the user asks for changes.
required_patterns: Review alone does not authorize edits
positive_prompts: Audit this skill for missed activation.
negative_prompts: Review this API schema.

triage-finding.original_description: Use when the user supplies or imports existing security findings, vulnerability reports, or security/vulnerability Jira/Linear tickets from scanners, advisories, GitHub, Atlassian Rovo, Linear, or similar backlog sources and wants static repo-impact triage. Do not use for discovery, duplicate-bug triage, validation, or fixes.
positive_prompts: Assess this imported vulnerability report for repository impact.
negative_prompts: Validate and fix this vulnerability.

gdpr.original_description: Apply GDPR-compliant engineering practices across your codebase. Use this skill whenever you are designing APIs, writing data models, building authentication flows, implementing logging, handling user data, writing retention/deletion jobs, designing cloud infrastructure, or reviewing pull requests for privacy compliance. Trigger this skill for any task involving personal data, user accounts, cookies, analytics, emails, audit logs, encryption, pseudonymization, anonymization, data exports, breach response, CI/CD pipelines that process real data, or any question framed as "is this GDPR-compliant?". Inspired by CNIL developer guidance and GDPR Articles 5, 25, 32, 33, 35.
positive_prompts: Design an authentication API.
Review our breach response processing.
negative_prompts: Adjust a Blender light with no user data.

needs.original_description: Use when the user asks to plan customer or stakeholder research, analyze interview notes, uncover workflows and unmet needs, or elicit requirements before choosing a solution. Do not trigger merely to clarify the current user's prompt, write a formal specification, or validate enthusiasm for an already-decided idea.
positive_prompts: Plan stakeholder research.
negative_prompts: Clarify this single coding prompt.

control-in-app-browser.original_description: Control the in-app Browser for opening, navigating, inspecting visible or interactive page state, clicking, typing, screenshots, and local web testing. It can have existing signed-in sessions. For semantic operations on linked resources, prefer a purpose-built connector, API, or CLI when available.
positive_prompts: Inspect the visible page in the in-app browser.
negative_prompts: Use the available dedicated CLI to retrieve a linked resource.

teach.original_description: Explain a body of work plainly so a person actually understands it. Runs the `how` and `why` skills and weaves what they find into one clear explanation. Use for 'teach me this', 'help me really understand X', 'explain this change or subsystem to me'.
positive_prompts: Explain this unfinished subsystem so I understand it.
Help me understand how a worktree shares history but keeps files separate.
Explain the effect of changing these inputs with an interactive example.
Teach this mechanism; choose a video if motion makes it clearer.
negative_prompts: Give only a one-line completion status.

publish-artifact-to-sites.original_description: Publish a validated Data Analytics report or dashboard artifact through Sites. Use automatically for durable artifacts in any positively identified Work Mode when the full Sites lifecycle is callable, or in ChatGPT Desktop outside Work Mode only after an explicit Sites request or acceptance of the optional post-handoff sharing offer.
required_patterns: Desktop outside Work Mode.*explicit Sites request or accepted sharing offer
positive_prompts: Publish this validated report through Sites in Desktop.
negative_prompts: Publish from Desktop without a request or accepted offer.

video.original_description: Create narrated explanatory animations with a local Manim, Piper and FFmpeg pipeline. Use for video explainers or when motion and narration improve understanding. Exclude general video editing and publication.
required_patterns: Exclude general video editing and publication
positive_prompts: Create a Dutch animation explaining Git worktrees.
Use a narrated video to show how the mechanism moves.
negative_prompts: Trim the first ten seconds from this recording.
Publish this movie to YouTube.
Answer this arithmetic question in one sentence.

new-repo.original_description: Bootstrap new NostraDavid repositories, or apply their repository baseline on request, with Just, Nix, prek, locked dependencies, and quality gates. Exclude ordinary feature work and unrelated repositories.
positive_prompts: Maak een nieuwe NostraDavid repo voor een kleine Python CLI met onze standaard tooling.
Breng deze repository op onze NostraDavid-basis met Just, Nix en prek.
negative_prompts: Los alleen deze bug in de bestaande API op.
Werk een dependency bij in een externe repository.
Leg uit wat een Justfile doet.
